headline: Willson Contreras Sparks Emotional Victory As Red Sox Roll At Fenway
morning_brew: What a wild night at Fenway Park. Willson Contreras absolutely crushed a ball, gave us a bat flip for the ages, and got himself tossed from the game. Talk about playing with some serious fire. He was emotional out there, thinking about his home country of Venezuela after those earthquakes, and honestly, you gotta love that kind of passion. Ranger Suarez was solid on the mound too, giving us six strong innings and racking up eight strikeouts to lock down the win. The bullpen shut the door, and we walked away with a six to three victory over the Washington Nationals.

This makes five wins in a row for the Sox, and even though we're still sitting at thirty-seven and forty-six, this streak is giving us some life. Pops always said that if you don't play with heart, you don't belong in Boston, and Contreras showed plenty of it. Anthony Seigler had himself a night too, picking up two hits to keep his average sitting at a scorching .361. If this lineup can keep finding ways to produce, maybe this summer won't be a total wash after all.

Down in Foxborough, negotiations are still ongoing to get cornerback Christian Gonzalez locked up on an extension before camp kicks off. We can't afford to have our best defensive back holding out when training camp is right around the corner. Over on the hardwood, the Celtics are looking at a quiet entry into free agency given their tight cap situation under the second apron, and Brad Stevens will need to find some bargain depth to help support Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. For the Bruins, the focus turns to the opening of NHL free agency tomorrow to see if they can finally address their scoring needs after that first-round exit.

news_digest.headline: Mindful of Venezuela, Contreras' emotion spills over in bat flip
news_digest.dans_take: You cannot help but respect the passion Contreras showed out there during a tough time.
